primary_claim: Decomposing refusal and sycophancy steering vectors with SAE features via inference-time optimization (gradient pursuit) in Phi-3 Mini finds a small number of interpretable features that reconstruct, and for refusal even surpass, the original steering vectors' behavioral effects without sacrificing MMLU performance; a single 'truthful' SAE feature extracted from a sycophancy vector classifies correct vs. incorrect MMLU answers at 56.1% accuracy (roughly Llama-2 13B level), but this effect does not replicate on TruthfulQA.

effect.metric: accuracy of a single SAE feature as a correct/incorrect MMLU-answer classifier
effect.value: 56.1% (Phi-3 Mini's own MMLU accuracy is 68.8%; 56.1% is roughly Llama-2 13B level); does not replicate on TruthfulQA

contradicts_or_qualifies: Builds on and improves upon the authors' own prior work applying ITO/gradient pursuit to in-context-learning steering vectors 'with less success'; refusal and sycophancy vectors reconstruct better

SAE reconstruction of MELBO-derived steering vectors achieves only mixed/weak success, in contrast to the stronger refusal and sycophancy results, and the authors say they are unlikely to continue this direction
stated_future_work: Publish the Sparse Feature Circuits findings on in-context-learning tasks (currently in preparation for arXiv)
limitations_stated: Refusal vector reconstruction results may not be robust: the original vector came from an SVD on weights (possibly not the best refusal vector to reconstruct), results worsen with more or fewer SAE features, and evaluation used just one judge model (LLaMA Guard) on 100 samples
No sparse combination of SAE features could reproduce sycophancy steering results for Gemma or Gemma 2
The MMLU 'truthful' feature classifier result does not replicate on TruthfulQA, where sycophancy features are much weaker classifiers
MELBO vector reconstruction results are weak overall, and the authors do not plan to continue pursuing this direction
Synthetic training data for the SAEs subjectively contains more repeated tokens in context than natural datasets, raising concerns about SAE training quality
quote: reconstructed SAE vectors surpass the original vectors and get close to optimized vectors in quality without sacrificing MMLU performance.
